source_text: Καὶ ὅτι διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ λαοῦ ὑμῶν καὶ διὰ τὰς εἰδωλολατρείας, ἀλλ᾿ οὐ διὰ τὸ ἐνδεὴς εἶναι τῶν τοιούτων προσφορῶν, ἐνετείλατο ὁμοίως ταῦτα γίνεσθαι, ἀκούσατε πῶς περὶ τούτων λέγει διὰ Ἀμώς, ἑνὸς τῶν δώδεκα, βοῶν· Οὐαὶ οἱ ἐπιθυμοῦντες τὴν ἡμέραν τοῦ κυρίου. Ἵνα τί αὕτη ὑμῖν ἡ ἡμέρα κυρίου: Καὶ αὐτή ἐστι σκότος καὶ οὐ φῶς. Ὅν τρόπον ὅταν ἐκφύγῃ ἄνθρωπος ἐκ προσώπου τοῦ λέοντος, καὶ συναντήσῃ αὐτῷ ἡ ἄρκτος, καὶ εἰσπηδήσῃ εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀπερείσηται τὰς χεῖρας αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ τὸν τοῖχον, καὶ δάκῃ αὐτὸν ὁ ὄφις. Οὐχὶ σκότος ἡ ἡμέρα τοῦ κυρίου καὶ οὐ φῶς, καὶ γνόφος οὐκ ἔχων φέγγος αὐτῆς; Μεμίσηκα, ἀπῶσμαι τὰς ἑορτὰς ὑμῶν, καὶ οὐ μὴ ὀσφρανθῶ ἐν ταῖς πανηγύρεσιν ὑμῶν. Διότι ἐὰν ἐνέγκητέ μοι τὰ ὁλοκαυτώματα καὶ τὰς θυσίας ὑμῶν, οὐ προσδέξομαι αὐτὰ καὶ σωτηρίου ἐπιφανείας ὑμῶν οὐκ ἐπιβλέψομαι. Ἀπόστησον ἀπ᾿ ἐμοῦ πλῆθος ᾠδῶν σου καὶ ψαλμῶν· ὀργάνων σου οὐκ ἀκούσομαι. Καὶ κυλισθήσεται ὡς ὕδωρ κρίμα καὶ ἡ δικαιοσύνη ὡς χειμάρρους ἄβατος. Μὴ σφάγια καὶ θυσίας προσηνέγκατέ μοι ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ, οἶκος Ἰσραήλ; λέγει κύριος. Καὶ ἀνελάβετε τὴν σκηνὴν τοῦ Μολὸχ καὶ τὸ ἄστρον τοῦ θεοῦ ὑμῶν Ῥαφάν, τοὺς τύπους, οὓς ἐποιήσατε ἑαυτοῖς. Καὶ μετοικιῶ ὑμᾶς ἐπέκεινα Δαμασκοῦ, λέγει κύριος· ὁ θεὸς ὁ παντοκράτωρ ὄνομα αὐτῷ. Οὐαὶ οἱ κατασπαταλῶντες Σιὼν καὶ τοῖς πεποιθόσιν ἐπὶ τὸ ὄρος Σαμαρείας. Οἱ ὠνομασμένοι ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀρχηγοῖς ἀπετρύγησαν ἀρχὰς ἐθνῶν· εἰσῆλθον ἑαυτοῖς οἶκος Ἰσραήλ. Διάβητε πάντες εἰς Χαλάνην καὶ ἴδετε, καὶ πορεύθητε ἐκεῖθεν εἰς Ἀμὰθ τὴν μεγάλην, καὶ κατάβητε ἐκεῖθεν εἰς Γὲθ τῶν ἀλλοφύλων, τὰς κρατίστας ἐκ πασῶν τῶν βασιλειῶν τούτων, εἰ πλείονά ἐστι τὰ ὅρια αὐτῶν τῶν ὁρίων ὑμῶν. Οἱ ἐρχόμενοι εἰς ἡμέραν πονηράν, οἱ ἐγγίζοντες καὶ ἐφαπτόμενοι σαββάτων ψευδῶν, οἱ κοιμώμενοι ἐπὶ κλινῶν ἐλεφαντίνων καὶ κατασπαταλῶντες ἐπὶ ταῖς στρωμναῖς αὐτῶν, οἱ ἐσθίοντες ἄρνας ἐκ ποιμνίων καὶ μοσχάρια ἐκ μέσου βουκολίων γαλαθηνά, οἱ ἐπικροτοῦντες πρὸς τὴν φωνὴν τῶν ὀργάνων, ὡς ἑστῶτα ἐλογίσαντο καὶ οὐχ ὡς φεύγοντα, οἱ πίνοντες ἐν φιάλαις οἶνον καὶ τὰ πρῶτα μύρα χριόμενοι, καὶ οὐκ ἔπασχον οὐδὲν ἐπὶ τῇ συντριβῇ τοῦ Ἰωσήφ. Διὰ τοῦτο νῦν αἰχμάλωτοι ἔσονται ἀπὸ ἀρχῆς δυναστῶν τῶν ἀποικιζομένων, καὶ μεταστραφήσεται οἴκημα κακούργων, καὶ ἐξαρθήσεται χρεμετισμὸς ἵππων ἐξ Ἐφραΐμ . Καὶ πάλιν διὰ Ἱερεμίου· Συναγάγετε τὰ κρέα ὑμῶν καὶ τὰς θυσίας καὶ φάγετε, ὅτι οὔτε περὶ θυσιῶν ἢ σπονδῶν ἐνετειλάμην τοῖς πατράσιν ὑμῶν, ῄ ἡμέρᾳ ἐπελαβόμην τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῶν ἐξαγαγεῖν αὐτοὺς ἐκ γῆς Αἰγύπτου [JÉR., VII, 21-22]. Καὶ πάλιν διὰ Δαυΐδ ἐν τεσσαρακοστῷ ἐνάτῳ ψαλμῷ οὕτως ἔφη· Θεὸς θεῶν κύριος ἐλάλησε, καὶ ἐκάλεσε τὴν γῆν ἀπὸ ἀνατολῶν ἡλίου μέχρι δυσμῶν. Ἐκ Σιὼν ἡ εὐπρέπεια τῆς ὡραιότητος αὐτοῦ. Ὁ θεὸς ἐμφανῶς ἥξει, ὁ θεὸς ἡμῶν, καὶ οὐ παρασιωπήσεται· πῦρ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ καυθήσεται, καὶ κύκλῳ αὐτοῦ καταιγὶς σφόδρα. Προσκαλέσεται τὸν οὐρανὸν ἂνω καὶ τὴν γῆν τοῦ διακρῖναι τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ. Συναγάγετε αὐτῷ τοὺς ὁσίους αὐτοῦ, τοὺς διατιθεμένους τὴν διαθήκην αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ θυσίαις. Καὶ ἀναγγελοῦσιν οἱ οὐρανοὶ τὴν δικαιοσύνην αὐτοῦ, ὅτι θεὸς κριτής ἐστιν. Ἄκουσον, λαός μου, καὶ λαλήσω σοι, Ἰσραήλ, καὶ διαμαρτυροῦμαί σοι· ὁ θεός, ὁ θεός σου εἰμὶ ἐγώ. Οὐκ ἐπὶ ταῖς θυσίαις σου ἐλέγξω σε· τὰ δὲ ὁλοκαυτώματά σου ἐνώπιόν μου ἐστὶ διὰ παντός. Οὐ δέξομαι ἐκ τοῦ οἴκου σου μόσχους οὐδὲ ἐκ τῶν ποιμνίων σου χιμάρους, ὅτι ἐμά ἐστι πάντα τὰ θηρία τοῦ ἀγροῦ, κτήνη ἐν τοῖς ὄρεσι καὶ βόες· ἔγνωκα πάντα τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ὡραιότης ἀγροῦ μετ᾿ ἐμοῦ ἐστιν. Ἐὰν πεινάσω, οὐ μή σοι εἴπω· ἐμὴ γάρ ἐστιν ἡ οἰκουμένη καὶ τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς. Μὴ φάγωμαι κρέα ταύρων. ἢ αἷμα τράγων πίωμαι; Θῦσον τῷ θεῷ θυσίαν αἰνέσεως. καὶ ἀπόδος τῷ ὑψίστῳ τὰς εὐχάς σου· καὶ ἐπικάλεσαί με ἐν ἡμέρᾳ θλίψεως, καὶ ἐξελοῦμαί σε, καὶ δοξάσεις με. Τῷ δὲ ἁμαρτωλῷ εἶπεν ὁ θεός· Ἵνα τί σὺ ἐκδιηγῇ τὰ δικαιώματά μου, καὶ ἀναλαμβάνεις τὴν διαθήκην μου διὰ στόματός σου; Σὺ δὲ ἐμίσησας παιδείαν καὶ ἐξέβαλες τοὺς λόγους μου εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω. Εἰ ἐθεώρεις κλέπτην, συνέτρεχες αὐτῷ, καὶ μετὰ μοιχοῦ τὴν μερίδα σου ἐτίθεις. Τὸ στόμα σου ἐπλεόνασε κακίαν, καὶ ἡ γλῶσσά σου περιέπλεκε δολιότητας. Καθήμενος κατὰ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου κατελάλεις, καὶ κατὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς μητρός σου ἐτίθεις σκάνδαλον. Ταῦτα ἐποίησας, καὶ ἐσίγησα· ὑπέλαβες ἀνομίαν ὅτι ἔσομαί σοι ὅμοιος. Ἐλέγξω σε καὶ παραστήσω κατὰ πρόσωπόν σου τὰς ἁμαρτίας σου. Σύνετε δὴ ταῦτα οἱ ἐπιλανθανόμενοι τοῦ θεοῦ, μήποτε ἁρπάσῃ, καὶ οὐ μὴ ᾖ ὁ ῥυόμενος. Θυσία αἰνέσεως δοξάσει με, καὶ ἐκεὶ ὁδός, ἥν δείξω αὐτῷ τὸ σωτήριόν μου . Οὔτε οὖν θυσίας παρ᾿ ὑμῶν λαμβάνει, οὔτε ὡς ἐνδεὴς τὴν ἀρχὴν ἐνετείλατο ποιεῖν, ἀλλὰ διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ὑμῶν. Καὶ γὰρ τὸν ναὸν τὸν ἐν Ἱερουσαλὴμ ἐπικληθέντα οὐχ ὡς ἐνδεὴς ὢν ὡμολόγησεν οἶκον αὐτοῦ ἢ αὐλήν, ἀλλ᾿ ὅπως καὶ κατὰ τοῦτο προσέχοντες αὐτῷ μὴ εἰδωλολατρῆτε. Καὶ ὅτι τοῦτό ἐστιν, Ἡσαΐας λέγει· Ποῖον οἶκον ᾠκοδομήσατέ μοι; λέγει κύριος. Ὁ οὐρανός μοι θρόνος, καὶ ἡ γῆ ὑποπόδιον τῶν ποδῶν μου .
pass_a_gloss: And because of the sins of your people and because of the idolatries, but not because He is in need of such offerings, He commanded these things to be done similarly; listen to how He speaks about these things through Amos, one of the twelve, crying out: Woe to those who desire the day of the Lord. Why is this day of the Lord to you? And this day is darkness and not light. Just as when a man escapes from the face of a lion, and a bear meets him, and he enters his house and leans his hands on the wall, and a snake bites him. Is not the day of the Lord darkness and not light, and gloom without its shining? I have hated, I have rejected your festivals, and I will not smell in your gatherings. For if you bring me your whole burnt offerings and your sacrifices, I will not accept them, and I will not look at the savior of your appearances. Turn away from me the multitude of your songs and psalms; I will not hear your instruments. And justice will roll like water, and righteousness like an uncontrollable stream. Did you not bring me sacrifices and offerings in the wilderness, house of Israel? says the Lord. And you took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, the types which you made for yourselves. And I will make you migrate beyond Damascus, says the Lord; the God, the Almighty, is His name. Woe to those who waste away Zion and to those who trust in the mountain of Samaria. Those who are named among the leaders have rebelled against the powers of the nations; the house of Israel has entered among them. Pass through all of you to Chalane and see, and go from there to Amath the great, and go down from there to Geth of the Philistines, the strongest of all these kingdoms, if their borders are greater than your borders. Those who come on an evil day, those who draw near and touch false sabbaths, those who sleep on ivory beds and waste away on their couches, those who eat lambs from the flocks and calves from the midst of the herds, fat ones, those who strike the strings of instruments, as if they were standing and not fleeing, those who drink wine in bowls and anoint themselves with the first myrrh, and they do not suffer anything at the crushing of Joseph. Therefore, now they will be captives from the beginning of the rulers of those being deported, and the dwelling of the wicked will be overturned, and the neighing of horses will be taken away from Ephraim. And again through Jeremiah: Gather your flesh and your sacrifices and eat, for I did not command your fathers concerning sacrifices or drink offerings on the day I took their hand to lead them out of the land of Egypt. And again through David in the forty-seventh psalm, he said thus: God of gods, the Lord spoke, and He called the earth from the rising of the sun to the setting. From Zion is the beauty of His goodness. God will come openly, our God, and He will not be silent; fire will burn before Him, and a storm will surround Him. He will call upon heaven above and the earth to judge His people. Gather to Him His holy ones, those who make His covenant through sacrifices. And the heavens will declare His righteousness, for God is a judge. Hear, my people, and I will speak to you, Israel, and I will testify against you: God, your God, I am. I will not rebuke you concerning your sacrifices; your whole burnt offerings are always before me. I will not accept from your house bullocks or from your flocks goats, for mine are all the animals of the field, cattle in the mountains and oxen; I know all the birds of the heaven, and the beauty of the field is with me. If I am hungry, I will not tell you; for mine is the world and its fullness. Shall I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats? Sacrifice a sacrifice of praise to God, and pay your vows to the Most High. And call upon me in the day of trouble, and I will deliver you, and you will glorify me. But to the sinner, God said: Why do you recite my righteousness, and take up my covenant with your mouth? You have hated discipline and cast my words behind you. If you saw a thief, you ran with him, and you placed your portion with an adulterer. Your mouth was full of evil, and your tongue was entwined with deceit. Sitting against your brother, you spoke against him, and against the son of your mother, you placed a stumbling block. You did these things, and I was silent; you thought lawlessness, that I would be like you. I will rebuke you and set your sins before your face. Understand these things, you who forget God, lest He seize, and there will be no deliverer. A sacrifice of praise will glorify me, and there I will show him my salvation. He does not receive sacrifices from you, nor did He command to do this because He is in need, but because of your sins. For He did not acknowledge the temple in Jerusalem, which is called by His name, as His house or court, because He is in need, but so that you, paying attention to this, would not idolize. And that this is so, Isaiah says: What house will you build for me? says the Lord. The heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool of my feet.

choices.why: The Greek word ὁμοίως indicates that God commanded these things to be done in a similar manner.
The Greek word ἐνετείλατο is in the third person singular, indicating that God is the one who commanded.

bible_refs.note: The Greek text only quotes 'Woe to those who desire the day of the Lord'

pass_b_english: God commanded these practices because of your people's sins and idolatry, not because He needs such offerings. Listen to how He addresses this through Amos, one of the twelve prophets, who cries out: Woe to you who long for the day of the Lord! Why do you want it? That day will be darkness, not light (Amos 5:18-20). It will be like a man who escapes a lion only to meet a bear, then leans his hand on the wall in his own house and is bitten by a snake. The day of the Lord is darkness, not light, a gloom with no brightness in it.

I hate and reject your festivals; I will take no pleasure in your solemn assemblies. Even if you bring Me burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them, nor will I look favorably on your peace offerings. Take away the noise of your songs; I will not listen to the music of your harps. Instead, let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream (Amos 5:21-24). Did you bring Me sacrifices and offerings those forty years in the wilderness, house of Israel? You carried the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, the idols you made for yourselves. So I will send you into exile beyond Damascus, says the Lord, whose name is God Almighty (Amos 5:25-27).

Woe to you who are complacent in Zion and feel secure on Mount Samaria, you notable men of the first nation, to whom the house of Israel comes! Cross over to Calneh and see; go from there to great Hamath, then down to Gath of the Philistines. Are their kingdoms better than yours, or their territory larger? (Amos 6:1-2). You put off the evil day and bring on a reign of violence. You lie on ivory beds, lounge on your couches, eat lambs from the flock and fattened calves from the stall. You strum on your harps like David and improvise on musical instruments. You drink wine by the bowlful and anoint yourselves with the finest oils, yet you do not grieve over the ruin of Joseph. Therefore you will be among the first to go into exile; your feasting and sprawling will end (Amos 6:3-7).

Through Jeremiah the Lord says: "Add your burnt offerings to your other sacrifices and eat the meat yourselves! For when I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, I did not speak to them or command them about burnt offerings and sacrifices" (Jeremiah 7:21-22).

David declares in Psalm 47: "God, the Lord of gods, has spoken; He summoned the earth from the rising of the sun to its setting. From Zion, perfect in beauty, God shines forth. Our God comes and will not be silent; a fire devours before Him, and around Him a tempest rages. He calls the heavens above and the earth to judge His people: 'Gather My faithful ones to Me, those who made a covenant with Me by sacrifice.' The heavens proclaim His righteousness, for God Himself is judge" (Psalm 47:1-6).

"Hear, My people, and I will speak; I will testify against you, Israel: I am God, your God. I do not rebuke you for your sacrifices or your burnt offerings, which are ever before Me. I have no need of a bull from your stall or goats from your pens, for every animal of the forest is Mine, and the cattle on a thousand hills. I know every bird in the mountains, and the insects in the fields are Mine. If I were hungry I would not tell you, for the world is Mine, and all that is in it. Do I eat the flesh of bulls or drink the blood of goats? Sacrifice thank offerings to God, fulfill your vows to the Most High, and call on Me in the day of trouble; I will deliver you, and you will honor Me" (Psalm 47:7-15).

But to the wicked God says: "What right have you to recite My laws or take My covenant on your lips? You hate My instruction and cast My words behind you. When you see a thief, you join with him; you throw in your lot with adulterers. You use your mouth for evil and harness your tongue to deceit. You sit and testify against your brother and slander your own mother's son. When you did these things and I kept silent, you thought I was exactly like you. But now I will rebuke you and lay the charge before you. Consider this, you who forget God, or I will tear you to pieces with no one to rescue you. Those who sacrifice thank offerings honor Me, and to the blameless I will show My salvation" (Psalm 47:16-23).

So God does not accept sacrifices from you, nor did He command them because He lacks anything, but because of your sins. He did not claim the temple in Jerusalem, which bears His name, as His house or court out of need, but so that by attending to it you would not turn to idolatry. Isaiah confirms this: "Heaven is My throne, and the earth is My footstool. What kind of house will you build for Me?" says the Lord (Isaiah 66:1).

review.notes: Pass B fails to preserve the agency and specific content of the Greek regarding the 'crushing of Joseph' and the 'neighing of horses'. Specifically, the Greek 'οὐκ ἔπασχον οὐδὲν ἐπὶ τῇ συντριβῇ τοῦ Ἰωσήφ' (they did not suffer anything at the crushing of Joseph) is rendered in Pass B as 'yet you do not grieve over the ruin of Joseph', which changes the subject/action. Furthermore, the Greek 'ἐξαρθήσεται χρεμετισμὸς ἵππων ἐξ Ἐφραΐμ' (the neighing of horses will be taken away from Ephraim) is rendered in Pass B as 'your feasting and sprawling will end', which is a significant departure from the literal text. Additionally, Pass B adds 'the cattle on a thousand hills' and 'the insects in the fields are Mine' which are not in the Greek source provided.
reasons: Pass B adds content not present in the Greek: 'the cattle on a thousand hills' and 'the insects in the fields are Mine'.
